A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CoVoGAN work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching of retained, revised, added, and removed material.

before.justification: v1 Section 6 and Appendix D report original generation benchmarks, control demonstrations, training-stability comparisons, and component ablations.

after.justification: v2 Section 5 and Appendix E retain original generation and control results and add diffusion-baseline evaluations and quantitative disentanglement results.

M1.justification: The described method retains the GRU, conditional component-wise Deep Sigmoid Flow, content MLP, StyleGAN2-ADA synthesis network, image/video discriminators, and mutual-information objective. Equations 5–6 and the architecture tables document the same procedure.

E1.justification: FaceForensics, SkyTimelapse, RealEstate, and their generation and latent-control tasks remain. v2 Figure 1 adds a small text-prompted head-turning test using Kling and Wan, introducing a different control-input scenario. The new quantitative disentanglement evaluation otherwise uses retained FaceForensics coverage.

E2.justification: v2 Table 1 retains the GAN comparators and adds VDM and LVDM on all three datasets, plus Latte on FaceForensics and SkyTimelapse. Latte also joins the computational-efficiency comparison in Table 6. This substantially expands comparison beyond the GAN-only benchmark in v1.

E3.justification: v1 assesses control qualitatively; v2 introduces a quantitative FaceForensics protocol using Dlib facial landmarks to derive eye size, mouth size, head position, and head angle, then evaluates representations with MCC, SAP, and modularity. These metrics also extend the existing ablations. The added Latte comparison uses released checkpoints; retained resolutions, splits, and hyperparameter settings are unchanged as reported.

E4.justification: The GRU-versus-RNN and flow-versus-MLP ablations expand from FVD alone in v1 Table A3 to explicit disentanglement measurements in v2 Table 3. Conversely, v1 Section 6.4 and Figure 6's RealEstate training-stability and collapse analysis are removed, not relocated. v2 Figure 1 also adds prompted-control failure cases for Kling and Wan.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests. v2 checklist item 7 explains that error bars are omitted because of computational expense, but introduces no uncertainty estimates or changed statistical reporting practice.

E6.justification: The original benchmark and ablation FVD values remain unchanged. Added results include Latte's SkyTimelapse FVD16 of 41.84, below CoVoGAN's retained 46.51, changing that table's leader. v2 Table 2 reports CoVoGAN MCC/SAP/modularity of 33.78/8.48/17.37%, exceeding both compared GANs. Table 3 adds disentanglement ablation scores, Table 6 adds Latte resource measurements, and the original training-stability results disappear.

T1.justification: v2's main blockwise theorem removes B4, the learned motion/content independence assumption, matching the appendix theorem already present in v1. The component-wise proof's explanation after Equation 15 replaces v1's unconditional-independence statements with conditional-independence statements. The definitions, theorem conclusions, and remaining derivations are substantially retained.

C1.justification: The method, identifiability, generation-quality, and controllability contributions remain. v2 removes superior robustness and computational efficiency from the headline contribution list and conclusion, although efficiency remains discussed in the appendix. The introduction broadens its superiority claim from GANs with similar backbones to video-generation models of similar scale.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly identifies integration with higher-fidelity generators and state-of-the-art text-to-video systems as unfinished work. Appendix A.2 adds discussion of subspace identification under partially satisfied assumptions, citing prior work. The results discussion acknowledges occasional diffusion-model fidelity advantages, while the earlier architectural explanation of training stability is removed.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents approximately 20 million training frames for convergence, Dlib-based annotation extraction, and use of released Latte checkpoints. Its checklist states that code is supplied in supplemental material, which the PDFs alone cannot verify. The A100 40 GB hardware disclosure and existing hyperparameter and architecture tables are retained.

R1.justification: New references include LVDM, Latte, Kling, Wan, the SAP and modularity sources, and Kong et al. on partial identifiability. These extend the contemporary comparison context and assumptions discussion. The existing nonlinear-ICA positioning and claimed first identifiability theorem for video generation remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The narrative is substantially reorganized: related work moves from main Section 2 to Appendix B, ablations move into main Section 5.4, and efficiency and impact discussions move to appendices. The introduction and conclusion are revised, and a lengthy NeurIPS checklist is added. These changes exceed localized language editing.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one. v2 adds the Kling/Wan figure and disentanglement table, expands benchmark and ablation tables, and relocates and expands the random-generation figure with diffusion samples. The efficiency table moves to the appendix and gains Latte, while the training-stability plot is removed. Existing control illustrations are largely retained.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens support for its central disentanglement claim through quantitative comparisons and matching ablations in Tables 2–3, where v1 relied mainly on visual examples. Broader baseline comparisons and explicit applicability limitations also help assessment. The net gain is limited by incompletely specified metric protocols, continued absence of statistical uncertainty, and removal of the training-stability evidence; the original CoVoGAN FVD results are unchanged.
